A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CQR/CMR efficiency study. Their text, equations, figures, table, and appendices support reliable comparison, including identification of material removed from v3.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendices C–D report original synthetic experiments, real-data evaluations, optimizer/model comparisons, and data-allocation analyses.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendices C–D retain original synthetic and real-data experimental results, including the optimizer, model, and data-allocation comparisons.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, SGD training, pinball objectives, CQR scores and calibration, and CMR's median/residual construction are unchanged. The alternative optimizers, losses, and neural models already appear in v2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic distributions and MEPS 19, MEPS 20, California Housing, cpusmall, and abalone datasets. Removing Appendix D.4's distribution diagnostics does not remove these datasets or their benchmark evaluations.

E2.justification: Figure 11 retains SGD, SGDM, Adam, and AdamW comparisons for CMR and CQR. Figure 12 retains linear, two-layer, and three-layer models. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Deleting Appendix D.4 removes its diagnostic protocol, including standardized feature histograms, QQ plots, and the heavy-tail classification threshold ξ > 0.25. The retained experiments' splits, training budgets, miscoverage grids, and length-deviation metric remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 removes the supplementary investigation of feature distributions and heavy tails in Appendix D.4, including the California Housing case study and Figures 14–18. Optimizer, nonlinear-model, alternative-loss, and data-allocation analyses remain.

E5.justification: The Hill-estimator tail-index estimation and reporting in Appendix D.4 are removed. Section 6 still reports 20 independent trials, and retained figures preserve their uncertainty displays; no change in repeated-run practices is documented.

E6.justification: V3 removes the distribution and tail-index findings in Figures 14–18, including ξ = 0.3 for California Housing's total rooms, total bedrooms, and population. Retained experimental results are unchanged, including Figure 3's −2.24 coefficient and Figure 5's 0.92 slope.

T1.justification: Section 2 removes the auxiliary set-valued quantile definition Qγ and its singleton condition while retaining the same canonical quantile qγ. The main assumptions, theorems, bounds, and appendix proofs remain substantively unchanged; other mathematical edits concern notation and numbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the joint dependence on training size, calibration size, and miscoverage, together with the same phase-transition and data-allocation claims.

C2.justification: Removing Appendix D.4 also removes its interpretation that consistent empirical deviations suggest CQR/CMR robustness to heavy-tailed features. Section 7's oracle-optimality and linearity limitations, and interpretations of retained experiments, remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 adds a reproducibility statement saying code, datasets, environment-setup scripts, experiment scripts, and figure-generation scripts accompany the submission. This is newly documented availability, without a public repository address. Deleted Appendix D.4 also loses its diagnostic feature-standardization note.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds discussions of Gauthier et al. (2025), Duchi (2025), and Joshi et al. (2025). Hill (1975) and Voitalov et al. (2019) disappear with the tail analysis. Publication-metadata updates to retained references do not change their identity.

P1.justification: Most prose and the section sequence remain intact. V3 shortens the quantile preliminaries, updates cross-references and the experimental roadmap, and adds ethics, reproducibility, funding, and Appendix E's language-model-use statements, alongside limited wording and affiliation edits.

P2.justification: The document is extensively retypeset into the ICLR format, changing typography, headings, spacing, and display placement. Figures 6–10 are redistributed and Figure 11 occupies a separate page. Figures 14–18 are removed; retained plots and Table 1 preserve their substantive contents.

improvement.justification: The central theory, proofs, benchmark evidence, and principal limitations remain intact. New related-work and reproducibility text modestly improves documentation, while deleting Appendix D.4 loses exploratory diagnostics and removes its associated robustness extrapolation. These peripheral tradeoffs and the extensive reformatting do not materially alter the paper's overall quality.
